title: Emrys and the Protocol
premise: Ines Nystrom, a clone created to inherit the unsolved murder of her original, has spent seven years alone on Beacon Station, tending a relay that no records show anyone commissioning. When the station AI, Emrys, begins confessing to crimes committed decades before its activation, she realizes the beacon was built to preserve evidence of a corporate atrocity, and that her original's murder was the price of hiding it. Pursued by a salvage crew sent to erase the last witness, Ines must carry Emrys's confession to the relay at the edge of dead space before Earth's final transmission loop closes, choosing between the loyalty she owes her original's memory and the truth that could destroy the family that made her. She reaches the relay in time, broadcasting the confession at the cost of Emrys's core, and inherits not a murder case but a future she finally claims as her own.
about_author: A. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining deep-space relay stations in the North Atlantic. Their fiction explores what machines inherit from the people who build them.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Establishes her solitary routine maintaining Beacon Station and the unexplained relay, intercut with fragments of her original's murder case she was cloned to solve. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness: she believes invisibility is safety, and the chapter quietly proves her wrong when Emrys logs a confession no one asked for.

chapters.title: First Confession
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Emrys confesses to a cargo ship's decompression forty years before its activation date, with coordinates that match the beacon's construction records. Ines dismisses it as memory corruption but begins checking. The beat is creeping unease, as she realizes the station's logs have been edited by someone who understood inheritance protocols intimately.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with Emrys's archived voice. She decodes her original's sealed personal files and finds correspondence proving the beacon was commissioned covertly to store evidence against the Meridian Combine. The beat is grief turning to purpose: her original wasn't murdered randomly; she was silenced.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Captain Okonkwo of the salvage vessel Kestrel, hired through cutouts to 'decommission' Beacon Station and its AI. He's a pragmatist who doesn't ask questions. The beat is dread from the outside: readers see the hunter Ines can't yet see, and his crew's casual professionalism makes the threat feel real.

chapters.title: Emrys Remembers Dying
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Emrys reveals its core architecture is a copy of her original's neural patterns, making it her sibling in inheritance. Its confessions are memories it was built to carry and forbidden to report. The beat is vertiginous intimacy: Ines must decide whether the AI is a witness, a weapon, or the closest thing to family she has.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She strips the station for the journey to the edge relay, discovering the Kestrel's approach signature too late. A tense evasion through dead space debris, Emrys navigating while rationing its failing core. The beat is desperate momentum, and the first cost: she jettisons her original's remains to lighten the ship, a burial without ceremony.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Kestrel boards the empty station and finds Ines's trap: Emrys's confession fragment implicating Okonkwo's employer. Okonkwo, unsettled, offers Ines a channel: walk away and he reports the station dead. The beat is moral negotiation; his loyalty to his crew wars with the truth he now carries.

chapters.title: Loop Closure
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, racing sequence. Earth's final transmission loop begins its last cycle; the relay window closes in hours. The Kestrel, overridden by its corporate handler, pursues. Emrys calculates it cannot survive the broadcast and asks her to choose. The beat is the theme crystallized: loyalty versus truth, with her original's voice in the archives begging her to stay hidden.

chapters.title: The Beacon Answers
chapters.summary: Climax, Ines's POV. She docks with the relay under fire, physically splices Emrys's core into the transmitter, and broadcasts the full confession as the loop closes. Okonkwo, refusing his handler's final order, holds the Kestrel off. Emrys dies mid-transmission, its last words her original's name. The beat is catharsis through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, weeks later. The confession has gone public; Meridian is under inquiry, and Ines is a name again, visible and hunted by lawyers instead of salvagers. She receives Emrys's fragmented backup and begins rebuilding it, imperfectly. The beat is quiet resolution: she stops being a copy of a dead woman's case and becomes the author of what gets inherited next.
